item.text: {"summary":"Draft is broadly publishable but needs clearer cited support for the 2025 inside-view update, an explicit model-prior statement, and a defensible interval basis.","requiredFixes":[{"rubricItem":"model_prior","severity":"warning","summary":"The draft uses a 2022-2024 average as a persistence prior but does not explicitly state whether a time-series/model prior was used or ruled out.","actionRequested":"Add one sentence naming the model prior, e.g. a persistence/three-year post-pandemic-regime mean, or explicitly state why no formal time-series model is used."},{"rubricItem":"update","severity":"warning","summary":"The movement from the 12.7 prior to 12.6 relies on claims about 2025 labor market, inflation, housing costs, transfers, and real income, but the cited public evidence is almost entirely Census release/table material rather than evidence for those 2025 conditions.","actionRequested":"Either cite public evidence for the 2025 labor/inflation/housing/transfer assumptions or reduce the inside-view adjustment and describe it as mostly persistence."},{"rubricItem":"interval","severity":"warning","summary":"The 80% interval is asserted as roughly -1.0/+1.2 points but is not tied to realized volatility, backtest error, survey error, or a stated subjective uncertainty calculation.","actionRequested":"State the empirical or subjective basis for the interval width, such as recent SPM year-to-year volatility excluding pandemic-transfer outliers plus added policy/measurement uncertainty."},{"rubricItem":"resolver","severity":"warning","summary":"The resolver is mostly clear, but the resolution date evidence is described in reasoning while the resolutionSourceUrl points only to the generic SPM tables page.","actionRequested":"Add the Census event-calendar URL or exact cited release-calendar evidence to the resolver/source context so the 2026-09-08 resolution date is auditable."}],"optionalSuggestions":["Clarify that the interval is an 80% interval to match confidence=0.8.","Make the upside and downside tail scenarios mention concrete approximate values outside the central interval."]}
